   121	
   122	    >>> graph.summarize.nodes(examples=False)
   123	    Type (3)        Count
   124	    ------------  -------
   125	    Protein            97
   126	    Complex            27
   127	    Abundance           2
   128	
   129	
   130	The number of nodes with each namespace can be summarized with ``BELGraph.summarize.namespaces()`` as in:
   131	
   132	.. code-block:: python
   133	
   134	    >>> graph.summarize.namespaces(examples=False)
   135	    Namespace (4)      Count
   136	    ---------------  -------
   137	    HGNC                  94
   138	    FPLX                   3
   139	    CHEBI                  1
   140	    TEXT                   1
   141	
   142	The edges can be summarized with ``BELGraph.summarize.edges()`` as in:
   143	
   144	.. code-block:: python
   145	
   146	    >>> graph.summarize.edges(examples=False)
   147	    Edge Type (12)                       Count
   148	    ---------------------------------  -------
   149	    Protein increases Protein               64
   150	    Protein hasVariant Protein              48
   151	    Protein partOf Complex                  47
   152	    Complex increases Protein               20
   153	    Protein decreases Protein                9
   154	    Complex directlyIncreases Protein        8
   155	    Protein increases Complex                3
   156	    Abundance partOf Complex                 3
   157	    Protein increases Abundance              1
   158	    Complex partOf Complex                   1
   159	    Protein decreases Abundance              1
   160	    Abundance decreases Protein              1
   161	
   162	Grounding the Graph
   163	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   164	Not all BEL graphs contain both the name and identifier for each entity. Some even use non-standard prefixes
   165	(also called **namespaces** in BEL). Usually, BEL graphs are validated against controlled vocabularies,
   166	so the following demo shows how to add the corresponding identifiers to all nodes.
   167	
   168	.. code-block:: python
   169	
   170	    from urllib.request import urlretrieve
   171	
   172	    url = 'https://github.com/cthoyt/selventa-knowledge/blob/master/selventa_knowledge/large_corpus.bel.nodelink.json.gz'
   173	    urlretrieve(url, 'large_corpus.bel.nodelink.json.gz')
   174	
   175	    import pybel
   176	    graph = pybel.load('large_corpus.bel.nodelink.json.gz')
   177	
   178	    import pybel.grounding
   179	    grounded_graph = pybel.grounding.ground(graph)
   180	
   181	Note: you have to install ``pyobo`` for this to work and be running Python 3.7+.
   182	
   183	Displaying a BEL Graph in Jupyter
   184	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   185	After installing ``jinja2`` and ``ipython``, BEL graphs can be displayed in Jupyter notebooks.
   186	
   187	.. code-block:: python
   188	
   189	   >>> from pybel.examples import sialic_acid_graph
   190	   >>> from pybel.io.jupyter import to_jupyter
   191	   >>> to_jupyter(sialic_acid_graph)
   192	
   193	Using the Parser
   194	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   195	If you don't want to use the ``pybel.BELGraph`` data structure and just want to turn BEL statements into JSON
   196	for your own purposes, you can directly use the ``pybel.parse()`` function.
   197	
   198	.. code-block:: python
   199	
   200	    >>> import pybel
   201	    >>> pybel.parse('p(hgnc:4617 ! GSK3B) regulates p(hgnc:6893 ! MAPT)')
   202	    {'source': {'function': 'Protein', 'concept': {'namespace': 'hgnc', 'identifier': '4617', 'name': 'GSK3B'}}, 'relation': 'regulates', 'target': {'function': 'Protein', 'concept': {'namespace': 'hgnc', 'identifier': '6893', 'name': 'MAPT'}}}
   203	
   204	This functionality can also be exposed through a Flask-based web application with ``python -m pybel.apps.parser`` after
   205	installing ``flask`` with ``pip install flask``. Note that the first run requires about a ~2 second delay to generate
   206	the parser, after which each parse is very fast.
   207	
   208	Using the CLI
   209	~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   210	PyBEL also installs a command line interface with the command :code:`pybel` for simple utilities such as data
   211	conversion. In this example, a BEL document is compiled then exported to `GraphML <http://graphml.graphdrawing.org/>`_
   212	for viewing in Cytoscape.
   213	
   214	.. code-block:: sh
   215	
   216	    $ pybel compile ~/Desktop/example.bel
   217	    $ pybel serialize ~/Desktop/example.bel --graphml ~/Desktop/example.graphml
   218	
   219	In Cytoscape, open with :code:`Import > Network > From File`.
